_meta.component: Risk Engine / Limiter — nics_risk_subsystem_spec_v1.3.md §2:42 (`rule manifest, two-phase gate, margin reservations, synthetic stops, protective flatten, net-liq survival watch, sole event-log writer, canonical position state`)
_meta.authority: nics_risk_subsystem_spec_v1.3.md §12A is the SEMANTIC authority for every knob below — name, default, meaning, and the cross-knob boot validation that must reject an invalid set 'before any strategy registers' (§12A:801-802). This file is the PHYSICAL layout only, per CLAUDE.md 'Per-module JSON configs only'. Where the two disagree, §12A wins and this file is wrong.
_meta.role_separation: CONFIG-ROLE ONLY (CLAUDE.md: 'config-role and data-role JSON stay separate'). The data-role expression of the §5 rule set — which rules run, in what order, in which phase — is NOT in this file and is not in this arc. Nothing here is a second behavioural authority: every value is a NUMBER, every word is under a `_`-prefixed documentation key that no loader reads, and the rules that consume these numbers live in the Limiter's own code.
_meta.lifecycle: §12.11 (`Config lifecycle (locked): boot-loaded, restart-only`) and §12A:801. Values load at BOOT and take effect only through restart. There is no reload verb anywhere on the load path — a mid-session change would let two decisions inside one open trade read different tunables. The config version is stamped into the Plane-1 boot event (§12.11), so every subsequent row is traceable to the exact tunable set it ran under. §6.3's baseline re-acceptance is the sole runtime-adaptive value and is explicitly STATE, not config.
_meta.not_implemented_here: Landing a knob as DATA is not implementing the rule that reads it. Stop conversion and trailing maintenance, protective-exit wiring, session-close flatten, full HALT semantics and auto-clear, cold-start reconciliation, the Sentinel, Scoring and the Allocator are all OUT of this arc; a value below existing proves only that the value has a home.
_meta.cc_calibrate: §12A:799-800 marks several of these placeholders until measured on node02 (§13). A CC-calibrate default here is a PLACEHOLDER with a stated direction of error, never a measured figure.
_meta.signal_max_age_ms: NOT a §12A knob — a Nix addition under the ARC 020 operator ruling for declared additions, flagged here exactly as `indeterminate` and `feed_lag()` are. §12A has no knob for the age of a STRATEGY signal because the frozen spec never asks the question: §6.4's staleness is about VENUE-sourced state and §4:210-212 bounds admission -> terminal feedback on the loop's own monotonic clock, not on the signal instant. CHECK-DEBT D3.463 opened the gap and the architect ruled it closed on the RESERVE seam (ARC 053): a reservation is §3's *taken at approval*, and approving capital against a signal of unbounded age is the one entry-side time quantity nothing in this tree refused. 5000 ms — deliberately LOOSER than `pending_ack_timeout_ms` (2000 ms) and tied to nothing else: the two bound different intervals (this one signal->approval, that one approval->ack) and deriving one from the other would assert a relationship neither the spec nor any measurement supports. The failure of too TIGHT a value is a denied entry on a healthy but slow path; the failure of too LOOSE a value is capital approved against a stale opinion. CC-calibrate against real strategy->Limiter latency once the bus exists. AN ABSENT `signal_ts` IS STALE, NOT NOW (§17): `scripts/limiterd.py` refuses the reserve rather than dating the signal at the instant it happened to arrive, which is what it did before this arc and is why D3.463 existed.

_derivations.deployable_pct: §12A:811 `DEPLOYABLE_PCT` = 0.70 — stated outright by the spec, not chosen here. §6.5:411 gives the same number as '30% buffer / 70% deployable — single number'.
_derivations.agg_margin_cap_pct: §12A:811 `AGG_MARGIN_CAP_PCT` = 0.70 of balance — stated outright. §6.5:412-413 is the rule it feeds: `Σ committed intraday margin (open + pending reservations + proposed) < 70% × balance`, hard, 100% of the time.
_derivations.netliq_safety_pad: §12A:812 `NETLIQ_SAFETY_PAD` — the spec gives the FORMULA and no number: force-flatten fires at `net_liq < Σ open margin × (1 + pad)`, ahead of the broker (§6.5:414-418). 0.25 is a CC-calibrate placeholder. Direction of error is stated because the two sides are not symmetric: too SMALL and Tradovate liquidates us first, which §6.5:418 forbids outright ('We never let the broker liquidate us'); too LARGE and we flatten profitable positions early, which costs money but never solvency. The placeholder therefore errs large.
_derivations.ledger_drift_tolerance_usd: §12A:813 `LEDGER_DRIFT_TOLERANCE` — reconcile drift that raises an audit event (§6.5:419, and the §11.7 periodic full-scan audit). CC-calibrate; 1.00 USD is a placeholder chosen so no fill-sized drift can hide under it — the smallest instrument in the §7:495 symbol scope is MES at a 1.25 USD tick value, so a tolerance below one tick cannot absorb a real execution, while cent-level rounding and commission arithmetic stay under it.
_derivations.eod_blackout_min: §12A:819 `EOD_BLACKOUT_MIN` = 20 — stated outright (global default, per-symbol override). §6.1:332-334 is the rule: no new entry from 15-20 min before that symbol's session close through its next session open.
_derivations.session_flatten_lead_min: §12A:820 `SESSION_FLATTEN_LEAD_MIN` = 10 — stated outright. §6.1b:340-342 is the rule: at this lead before each symbol's session close the Limiter force-flattens all open positions in that symbol, `reason=session`.
_derivations.session_flatten_lead_pad_min: NOT a §12A knob, and its absence is a finding rather than an omission here. §6.1b:346 states the boot-validated ordering invariant as `SESSION_FLATTEN_LEAD_MIN < EOD_BLACKOUT_MIN − pad` and §12A:821 repeats it, but §12A names no `pad` knob — so the one invariant §12A:802 singles out by name is UNEXECUTABLE as written. Landed as a declared Nix addition so the rule can run at all; 5 min is a placeholder that keeps 10 < 20 − 5. Recorded in docs/CHECK-DEBT.md.
_derivations.eod_blackout_min_by_symbol: NOT a §12A knob, and the distinction is the point. §12A:819 states the per-symbol override as a PROPERTY of the scalar knob (`EOD_BLACKOUT_MIN` = 20 '(per-symbol override)') and gives no knob NAME for the override table, so there is nothing to cite — the same shape as session_flatten_lead_pad_min below. The scalar `eod_blackout_min` above remains the SINGLE physical home of the §12A knob; this map holds DEVIATIONS ONLY. A symbol appears here only when its value differs from that default, so this file never carries a second copy of a value the scalar already owns (directive 3: do not restate a mutable fact). EMPTY today because no symbol has been CC-calibrated away from 20. §6.1b:346-348 is what needs it: the ordering invariant holds PER SYMBOL, so the validator judges the global pair PLUS every symbol named here, and a deviation that inverts the pair is rejected naming the symbol.
_derivations.session_flatten_lead_min_by_symbol: NOT a §12A knob, for the same reason as the map above: §12A:820 states '(per-symbol override)' as a property of `SESSION_FLATTEN_LEAD_MIN` and names no override knob. §12A:821 makes the lead 'CC-calibrate vs observed close liquidity/slippage', which is a PER-SYMBOL observation, so this is where those figures land once measured. DEVIATIONS ONLY, empty today, single-home rule as above.
_derivations.eow_blackout_min: §12A:822 `EOW_BLACKOUT_MIN` = 30 before Friday close — stated outright. §6.2:355-357 is the rule, with window union across overlapping blackouts.
_derivations.news_blackout_min: §12A:822 `NEWS_BLACKOUT_MIN` = 20 before scheduled event — stated outright. §6.3:360 is the leading (predictive, clock-driven) edge; the trailing edge is live margin and is not a clock knob.
_derivations.margin_elevated_pct: NOT a §12A knob, and its absence is a finding rather than an omission here — the same shape as `session_flatten_lead_pad_min` above. §6.3:361-362 makes the trailing edge 'hold until margin returns to baseline (+ min-time floor)' and gives no threshold for what counts as ABOVE baseline; a strict inequality on a live venue figure would trip on every rounding tick and never release. 0.10 is a CC-calibrate placeholder that errs SMALL: too small blocks entries that were safe, which costs opportunity; too large ignores a real 4x margin snap into the close (§6.1:335), which costs solvency. Landed by ARC 033 / Stage 1A and recorded in docs/CHECK-DEBT.md.
_derivations.margin_min_hold_s: NOT a §12A knob. §6.3:361-362 names the '+ min-time floor' on the trailing edge and gives it no name and no number, so the floor is unexecutable as the spec writes it. 300 s is a CC-calibrate placeholder chosen so a one-print dip in the venue's margin figure cannot reopen entries mid-event; it errs LARGE for the reason §6.3 gives the floor at all — the reactive edge without a floor is a rule that releases on noise. ARC 033 / Stage 1A; docs/CHECK-DEBT.md.
_derivations.margin_reacceptance_s: NOT a §12A knob. §6.3:363-365 is the anti-lockout clause — 'if margin holds stable-elevated beyond a defined period (regime shift, not spike), accept the new level as baseline — alert operator' — and 'a defined period' is the whole definition the spec gives. 3600 s is a CC-calibrate placeholder. Direction of error is asymmetric and stated: too SHORT re-baselines an ordinary spike and disarms §6.3's own trailing edge, too LONG leaves the system locked out longer after a permanent broker hike, and §6.3:365 forbids only the permanent case ('must never lock the system out forever'). It therefore errs LONG. Boot-validated against margin_min_hold_s inside nixrisk/blackout.py's BlackoutKnobs, not here — that cross-knob rule has no home in scripts/risk_config.py yet and the gap is a CHECK-DEBT row, not a silent default. ARC 033 / Stage 1A.
_derivations.pending_ack_timeout_ms: §12A:830 `PENDING_ACK_TIMEOUT_MS` (~1-2s) — 'status query, never resend'. The spec gives a RANGE, not a value; the upper end is taken because the failure of a too-short ack timeout is a spurious status query on every marketable order, and §4 makes the query the resolution path rather than an exception. CC-calibrate. THIS FILE IS THE SINGLE PHYSICAL HOME: risks/broker_order.config.json READS this value rather than restating it (ARC 020's `obligation_when_R2_lands`, honoured here).
_derivations.fill_timeout_ms: §12A:830 `FILL_TIMEOUT` — 'order-type-dependent'. CC-calibrate placeholder. Same single-home rule as the knob above: broker-order reads it here.
_derivations.go_timeout_s: §12A:831 `GO_TIMEOUT_T` — 'strategy resets to flat-and-free if no feedback within T'. CC-calibrate per §13 objective 10. The value 10 is not invented: nix_strategy_contract_v1.1.md §4.2 puts `go_timeout_s` in the platform's own REGISTER_ACK payload at 10, so the platform ISSUES this number to every strategy and it must have a physical home on the Nix side. §4:210-212 is the rule it feeds — the deadlock breaker on the one-in-flight lock.
_derivations.heartbeat_interval_s: §12A:832 `HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL` = 1s — stated outright, and matched by nix_strategy_contract_v1.1.md §4.6 ('Every `hb_interval_s` (default 1 s)') which the platform likewise issues at registration.
_derivations.heartbeat_miss_grace_cycles: §12A:832 `HEARTBEAT_MISS_GRACE` = 1 cycle before presumed-dead — stated outright. §4:260-261 is the rule: heartbeat miss ⇒ wait exactly one cycle (1s); a second consecutive miss ⇒ strategy presumed dead.
_derivations.halt_cooldown_floor_s: NOT a §12A knob, and its absence is a finding rather than an omission here — the same shape as `session_flatten_lead_pad_min` above. §12.5:632 states the rule outright ('Auto-set conditions may auto-clear on condition-clear + minimum floor (cooldown discipline)') and §12A names NO knob for that floor. The nearest thing it has is `COOLDOWN_MIN_TIME` at §12A line 839, which is §4:300-302's POST-PROTECTIVE cooldown, keyed by EXIT CLASS (discretionary / stop / uncertainty / margin_session), which is a different ladder for a different subject and is already landed above. Reusing it would make one number govern both how long a strategy waits after a stop and how long the whole system stays halted after a clock-skew event. Landed as a declared Nix addition so the §12.5:632 rule can run at all, keyed by the §12.5:631 CAUSE. `operator` is deliberately absent: §12.5:633 gives an operator HALT no auto-clear, so a floor for it would imply one exists — `scripts/nixrisk/halt.py` REFUSES to construct if the key appears. Every value is a CC-calibrate placeholder that errs LARGE, because the two directions are not symmetric: too short and the system resumes trading into a condition that has only just stopped flapping, too long and it sits flat, which costs opportunity and never solvency. The ladder mirrors §4:301's order — the fast-recovering data condition shortest, the ones that mean the system's own arithmetic or supervision was wrong the longest. Recorded in docs/CHECK-DEBT.md.
_derivations.cooldown_min_time_s: §12A:839 `COOLDOWN_MIN_TIME` — 'floor + condition-clear (hybrid), per exit class'. CC-calibrate. The KEYS are the exit classes §4:301 enumerates, transcribed rather than invented: 'Discretionary exit → none. Ordinary stop → short. Feed/uncertainty/stale → longer. Margin/session → longest or until condition clears.' The spec fixes the ORDER and not the seconds, so the ladder is boot-validated (rule `cooldown.ladder_is_ordered`) and the four numbers are placeholders. `discretionary` is 0 because §4:301 says 'none', which is a value and not a missing one.

_boot_validation.why: Every scalar knob outside the cooldown ladder must be > 0. §12A:801-802 requires boot validation to reject an invalid set before any strategy registers, and a zero or negative tunable on this module is a gate that cannot deny, a blackout with no width, or a timeout that expires instantly.
Every `_pct` knob is a fraction of balance and must lie in (0, 1]. A percentage above 1 would let the aggregate margin cap admit more than the whole account.

agg_margin_cap_pct must not exceed deployable_pct. §6.5:420 calls the 70% intraday cap and the blackout calendar 'one coupled system'; a margin cap wider than the deployable envelope would admit commitments the 30% buffer was reserved to protect.

session_flatten_lead_min < eod_blackout_min − session_flatten_lead_pad_min, PER SYMBOL. This is the ONE invariant §12A:802 names as boot-validated, stated at §6.1b:346-348: the entry blackout must lead the flatten deadline, and config validation REJECTS any per-symbol set violating it. Otherwise the system could open a position after the deadline that force-flattens it. ARC 033 / Stage 1 / B widened the rule from the single global pair to the global pair PLUS every symbol named in eod_blackout_min_by_symbol or session_flatten_lead_min_by_symbol, and every rejection NAMES the offending symbol: with per-symbol overrides in play, judging only the global pair would pass a set in which an individual symbol is inverted.

go_timeout_s must outlast pending_ack_timeout_ms. §4:210-212 arms the GO-timeout as a deadlock breaker for a LOST message; if it expires while the Limiter's own §4 pending-ack machinery is still resolving the same GO, the strategy resets to flat-and-free against a live order and the breaker fires on the healthy path.

heartbeat_miss_grace_cycles >= 1. §4:260-261 pins the grace at exactly one cycle before a second consecutive miss presumes death; a grace of zero makes one dropped beat a strategy death, and death recovery flattens positions.

discretionary <= stop <= uncertainty <= margin_session, with every class after discretionary strictly positive. §4:301 fixes the ORDER of the ladder ('none / short / longer / longest') and not the seconds, so the order is the checkable part.
